Hi Lena / FinOps —

Thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

Key notes from discovery:
- Primary use: customer support automation + knowledge retrieval for EU and US customers.
- Concern areas you raised: PII handling, embedding persistence, log telemetry sent to vendors, retention windows, and marketplace connectors that may route telemetry externally.
- Desired constraint: EU-only residency for customer-facing workloads where regulated data is involved.

Action items we offered on the call (and next steps):
1) Share our security pack and current subprocessor inventory (we'll attach these).
2) Clarify what telemetry leaves the platform versus what stays ephemeral (see question list below).
3) Review options: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (VPC) for EU residency and auditability.
4) Schedule a short technical deep-dive with Marissa (our security lead) + Neha (solutions/infra) to walk your security team through controls.

Quick clarifying questions for your security/FinOps team before the dive:
- Are embeddings considered regulated in your policy (i.e., are they treated as PII)?
- Do you have a maximum retention window we should pre-filter for (e.g., 30/90/365 days)?
- Any disallowed subprocessors (e.g., specific telemetry vendors or regions)?

Attachments I'll drop in the follow-up: Redwood_Security_Pack_2026.pdf and a current subprocessor inventory CSV.

Proposed times for a 45-min technical call next week: Wed 2026-12-08 09:00-11:00 PT or Thu 2026-12-09 13:00-16:00 PT — open to other slots.

I'll follow up with Marissa who can provide the technical answers below.

Thanks,
Karthik

Thanks, Karthik — helpful recap. A few clarifying items from our security and FinOps reviewers before we lock a follow-up: 

1) Telemetry scope: please confirm which of the following are sent off-platform to telemetry vendors or cloud logging: request/response tokens, raw user inputs, derived embeddings, model debug traces, error/stack traces. We need a clear mapping.
2) Embeddings: are embedding vectors persisted by default? If so, where and for how long? Are they encrypted at rest and accessed via KMS?
3) Retention: can we configure retention windows per workspace (30/90/365)? Do audit logs and query logs have separate retention?
4) Marketplace connectors: any marketplace partner integrations that perform outbound calls to third parties (e.g., analytics or transcription services)? How are those connectors authorized and audited?
5) Subprocessors: please provide names + regions for cloud providers and telemetry partners (we need EU-only where possible).
6) Contract: do you support contract language limiting third-party sharing for regulated customers (we will share a sample clause).

If you can get the security pack and the subprocessor CSV over, we'll pre-read and send a short list of redlines/questions. Prefer the technical call with Marissa once we have the attachments in-hand.

Regards,

Squadra Financial

Hi Lena / Squadra team —

Thanks for the detailed questions. Attaching the Redwood_Security_Pack_2026.pdf and redwood-subprocessors-2026.csv here. Below are concise answers to each numbered item so you can triage before the technical call.

1) Telemetry scope
- Request/response tokens: by default we do not persist raw request/response tokens unless customers opt-in for debugging. Transient tokenization artifacts exist in-memory at runtime and are not pushed to telemetry vendors.
- Raw user inputs: not persisted by default on Hosted; persistent storage is opt-in (e.g., for customer-specified logs or analytics).
- Derived embeddings: persistent storage is opt-in. If enabled, embeddings are stored in an encrypted vector store provisioned in the region you select.
- Model debug traces: collected only when debug mode is enabled and always redacted; we offer a gated support workflow to capture traces under an NDA.
- Error/stack traces: basic error telemetry (error codes, anonymized stack hashes) may be sent to our observability partner for platform reliability; payloads exclude raw PII.

2) Embeddings persistence & encryption
- Default: embeddings are ephemeral unless the customer enables persistent embeddings (via API/console setting).
- When persisted: vectors are encrypted at rest with customer-managed KMS option available (Private & Dedicated tiers).
- Retention: configurable; default for persisted embeddings is 365 days but we can set shorter windows (30/90) on request and automate deletion via lifecycle policies.

3) Retention controls
- Workspace-level retention configuration available for logs, prompts, and persisted embeddings (30 / 90 / 365 day presets + custom window via request).
- Audit logs and query logs are separated: audit logs retention is 365 days by default; query logs (user prompts/outputs) follow workspace retention if persisted.

4) Marketplace connectors
- Marketplace partners are treated as distinct subprocessors. Most connectors (indexing, search, retrieval plugins) operate in-customer region when requested; by default they do not forward telemetry outside the selected region.
- We can disable any connector's telemetry export on a per-customer basis and require an explicit contract for partners that need to export data.

5) Subprocessors & regions (summary)
- Cloud compute: AWS (us-east-1, eu-west-1), GCP (europe-west2), Azure (West Europe).
- Observability/telemetry partner: LogStream Inc. (EU-hosted nodes available), AnonMetrics (US/EU).
- Vector DB partner: VectorVault (offers EU-only tenancy).
- Full names and regions included in redwood-subprocessors-2026.csv (attached).

6) Contract language & redlines
- We support a data-sharing limitation clause for regulated customers. We can accept a narrow third-party sharing restriction or map required language into our Data Processing Addendum (DPA). Send your sample clause and legal can provide a proposed edit.

Operational options for stricter control:
- Private deployment (VPC or on-prem) with customer-managed KMS and no outside telemetry routing.
- Dedicated pools pinned to EU regions with SLA for throughput/latency.
- Canary feature to disable telemetry for production traffic and retain only aggregated metrics.

Next steps:
- I can run a 45-min technical review for your security team. Proposed slots: Wed 2026-12-08 16:00-16:45 ET or Thu 2026-12-09 10:00-10:45 ET. Please pick one and I will send a calendar invite.
- If you have contract language, upload to the HubSpot deal link and tag Karthik + our legal queue.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Head of Security & Compliance | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

Hi Lena — quick answers to your two clarifications: 

1) Embeddings (EU-only guarantee)
- Yes. When persistent embeddings are enabled and the customer selects EU residency, we provision an EU-only vector store (VectorVault EU tenancy) and enforce deletion policies through lifecycle jobs. We can include an EU-only storage guarantee in the DPA with related controls (encryption, access logs).

2) Telemetry (disablement)
- Yes. For Dedicated and Private deployments we provide a configuration to disable outbound telemetry to third-party observability vendors. For Hosted customers we offer a telemetry opt-out that restricts exports and limits data to aggregated, anonymized metrics; fully disabling all telemetry requires Dedicated/Private or an agreed contractual exception.

Pricing ballpark (for FinOps)
- Dedicated EU reserved pool: approx $X,XXX/month per vGPU equivalent (exact pricing depends on commit term and throughput requirements). We will provide a tailored estimate once we have expected qps and model selection.

Next steps: I'll send a calendar invite for Wed 2026-12-08 16:00 ET for the technical walkthrough with Marissa + Karthik. Please share any contract redlines to the HubSpot deal link ahead of the call.
